events.title: Servius Tullius celebrates a triumph over the Etruscans
events.description: According to the Fasti Triumphales, Servius Tullius, by tradition the sixth king of Rome, celebrated the first of three triumphs over the Etruscans. He is said to have routed a great Etruscan army early in his reign.
events.html: According to the Fasti Triumphales, Servius Tullius, by tradition the sixth king of Rome, celebrated the first of three triumphs over the Etruscans. He is said to have routed a great Etruscan army early in his reign.

events.title: Malcolm II of Scotland dies
events.description: Malcolm II died after a 29-year reign and was succeeded by his grandson Duncan I. Duncan was killed in battle by Macbeth in 1040, events Shakespeare reworked freely more than five centuries later.

events.title: The White Ship sinks off Barfleur, drowning William Adelin
events.description: The White Ship sank in the English Channel off Barfleur, drowning William Adelin, heir to Henry I of England; of some 300 aboard, only a butcher from Rouen survived. William's death led to the Anarchy.
events.html: The White Ship sank in the English Channel off Barfleur, drowning William Adelin, heir to Henry I of England; of some 300 aboard, only a butcher from Rouen survived. William's death led to the Anarchy.

events.title: Baldwin IV of Jerusalem routs Saladin at Montgisard
events.description: The young King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem, a leper since childhood, with a small force of knights including Raynald of Châtillon, surprised and routed Saladin's much larger army near Ramla. Saladin narrowly escaped back to Egypt.
events.html: The young King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem, a leper since childhood, with a small force of knights including Raynald of Châtillon, surprised and routed Saladin's much larger army near Ramla. Saladin narrowly escaped back to Egypt.

events.title: Boabdil agrees to surrender Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella
events.description: Muhammad XII (Boabdil) agreed in the Treaty of Granada to surrender Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella, who guaranteed the Muslims their religion, law and property. The city was handed over on 2 January 1492; the promises were broken within a decade.

events.title: The last British troops leave New York City
events.description: British forces evacuated New York, their last stronghold in the United States, and George Washington led the Continental Army into the city. 'Evacuation Day' was celebrated in New York for over a century.

events.title: Union troops storm Missionary Ridge
events.description: At Chattanooga, Union soldiers charged up Missionary Ridge beyond their orders and routed Braxton Bragg's Confederate army. The victory opened the way into Georgia.
events.html: At Chattanooga, Union soldiers charged up Missionary Ridge beyond their orders and routed Braxton Bragg's Confederate army. The victory opened the way into Georgia.

events.title: Hollywood studios blacklist the 'Hollywood Ten'
events.description: Studio heads issued the Waldorf Statement, refusing to employ ten writers and directors cited for contempt of Congress. The Hollywood blacklist that followed ended or interrupted hundreds of careers.

events.title: Suriname gains independence from the Netherlands
events.description: The former colony of Dutch Guiana on South America's north coast became the independent Republic of Suriname. Around a third of its population emigrated to the Netherlands.
